clue.text: Standard raised across the Channel?

parts.note: a standard is a flag, and the one hoisted on the far side of the English Channel is the French national flag of three colours

explanation.surface: A query about some benchmark or norm being lifted on the other side of the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' reads as a norm, but it is a flag; 'across the Channel' points from Britain to France, whose flag is the blue, white and red one.
explanation.definitionFit: The French national flag is the classic three-coloured banner, a standard flown in France.

clue.text: Back the other side

definitions.meaning: to back a car is to drive it backwards
the rear or opposite face of a coin or sheet

explanation.definitionFit: To back a car is to drive it backwards, and the other side of a coin or page is its flip side.

clue.text: Pretender ignores one calling aloud

indicators.note: ignores says the letter for one is left out of the pretender word

parts.note: a pretender is a claimant to a throne
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rival for the throne refuses to notice one person shouting out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignores' removes I from CLAIMANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamant is a literary adjective for insistently loud or clamorous, shouting out.

clue.text: See work difficulty as means of escape

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
op, short for opus, is a musical work
being in a hole means being in difficulty

explanation.surface: Someone views a hard job as a way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lo' is archaic for 'look, see'; OP is opus, a numbered composition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap in a rule lets someone evade it, so it is a way out of an obligation.

clue.text: Send back to prison the chap overdrawn, apparently

indicators.note: apparently says to picture the chap as 'in the red', so his word sits inside the overdrawn word

parts.note: an overdrawn account is in the red
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: A judge returns to jail the fellow whose bank account seems to be overdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Being overdrawn is being 'in the red'; 'apparently' asks the solver to picture the chap literally inside that colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that orders an accused person kept in custody until trial sends them back to jail.

clue.text: Notice illumination giving full public attention

parts.note: to spot is to notice
light is illumination

explanation.surface: A sign showing lighting that puts someone in the public eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Being the focus of public interest is being in the glare, the centre of attention.

clue.text: Sagacious, well-mannered for the most part and in charge

indicators.note: for the most part says the courteous word loses its final letter

parts.note: polite means well-mannered

explanation.surface: A description of a wise person who is courteous and usually in control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' cuts POLITE to POLIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Politic means prudent and shrewd, wise in judgement, so it matches sagacious.

clue.text: Top up helpers in cast

indicators.note: cast means thrown about, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Extra assistants are taken on to boost a theatre company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like actors, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To refill or restock something is to top it up, a synonym.

clue.text: Go off and walk in river

indicators.note: in says the walking word sits inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
to plod is to walk heavily

explanation.surface: Someone leaves and takes a stroll through a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The EXE is a river in south-west England, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb that goes off bursts, so the two phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: One flying from Barcelona via Torremolinos

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the run of letters in the place names that follow

explanation.surface: A traveller flying from Barcelona to the Costa del Sol via Torremolinos.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the last A of Barcelona through via into the start of Torremolinos.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is a person who flies an aircraft, so the phrase describes one.

clue.text: Rising of industrious workers

parts.note: a rising is a small hill, and the industrious workers are ants, so this is the mound such insects build

explanation.surface: It sounds like a revolt by hard-working labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' suggests an uprising of workers, but it is a mound of earth; the industrious workers are ants.
explanation.definitionFit: Ants heap up soil into a mound around their nest, a small rise of their making.

clue.text: The best instrument filled pastry

parts.note: the cream of something is its best part
a horn is a brass instrument

explanation.surface: A boast that some instrument is the finest, then a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: A cream horn is a British cone of puff pastry filled with whipped cream.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cone-shaped puff pastry case piped full of cream, a kind of filled pastry.

clue.text: Shine as a result of help turning up in class

indicators.note: in says the reversed help word goes inside the class word

parts.note: rate means class, as in first-rate

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue says the help word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: A pupil glows because of the help that arrived in class.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turning up' reads the help word from bottom to top; 'in' then places it within the class word. Rate means class, as in first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: To give off light or glow outward is to beam, a synonym for shine.

clue.text: Something put on caught out of harmful habit

indicators.note: out of says the letter for caught is taken away from the habit word

parts.note: an addiction is a harmful habit
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Something taken on or acquired after one has been caught out of a bad habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes C from ADDICTION.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is something added or put on, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Wives talked about 'Like a Virgin'

indicators.note: about here means 'in and around', so the answer is found lying within the words wives talked

explanation.surface: Wives chatting about the Madonna song Like a Virgin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talked about' looks like a homophone signal, but 'about' marks letters lying in 'Wives talked'.
explanation.definitionFit: The vestal virgins were chaste priestesses of ancient Rome, so the adjective means chaste, like a virgin.

clue.text: Five show support

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
to indicate is to show

explanation.surface: Five people demonstrate their backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To vindicate a claim is to justify or back it up, so the verb means support.

clue.text: Point of attack a rower had changed

indicators.note: changed says the letters are altered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A rower had a change of plan at the point of attack.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed tip of an arrow is the part that strikes, the head of an attack.

clue.text: Revival of interest in second delivery?

definitions.meaning: a renewal or renaissance of something that had faded
read literally, a birth for the second time, with the question mark flagging the whimsy

explanation.surface: A fresh wave of interest in a parcel being delivered again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' suggests the post, but it is a birth: being born again.
explanation.definitionFit: A renaissance is a renewal of life or interest, and a second birth renews life literally.

clue.text: Picture pretty as could be

indicators.note: could be suggests these letters may take another possible arrangement

explanation.surface: A painting described as pretty as could be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' says the letters of 'pretty as' could become something else.
explanation.definitionFit: A woven wall hanging depicts a scene, so it is a kind of picture.

clue.text: Shock — divas to underwhelm in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A jolt: some prima donnas set out to disappoint.
explanation.definitionFit: To amaze or stun someone is to give them a shock, a synonym.

clue.text: Fasten case? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite says the case word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: an ...é case is a slim briefcase

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to fasten a case and is told not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last letter from ATTACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix or secure one thing to another is to fasten it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Growing attachment?

parts.note: sounds like a deepening fondness, but it is the slender coil a climbing plant uses to cling while it grows

explanation.surface: It suggests an affection getting stronger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attachment' reads as fondness, but it is a physical fastening a growing plant makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing plant's thin coiling shoot wraps round a support and holds the plant to it.

clue.text: Band opposing Ronald in support of revolutionary

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece supporting another sits beneath it, so these letters follow the revolutionary

parts.note: Che Guevara is the crossword revolutionary
V, short for versus, means opposing
Ron is short for Ronald

explanation.surface: A band set against Ronald yet backing a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'in support of' puts V and RON below CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevron is a V-shaped stripe, such as a band on a uniform sleeve.

clue.text: Get off one's high horse?

parts.note: the idiom means to stop acting superior, but read literally it is climbing down from a tall mount

explanation.surface: An appeal to someone to stop being so arrogant.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is taken literally: get down from a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb down from a horse or bicycle is the literal sense of getting off it.

clue.text: Talk as sailor leaves one who croaks

indicators.note: leaves says the sailor word departs from the creature's name

parts.note: the natterjack is a European toad, a croaking creature
jack is a sailor, as in jack tar

explanation.surface: Chatter as a seaman leaves someone who complains.
explanation.walkthrough: The natterjack is a toad found in Britain; 'one who croaks' looks like a grumbler, or someone dying.
explanation.definitionFit: To chat idly is to natter, a British informal word for talk.

clue.text: Mainly it separates Greece from Turkey

definitions.text: Mainly it separates Greece from Turkey

parts.words: Mainly it separates Greece from Turkey
parts.note: the main is an old word for the sea, so 'mainly' hints that the divider is a body of water between the two countries

explanation.surface: A geography note: what chiefly divides Greece from Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' seems to mean 'chiefly', but it puns on 'the main', poetic for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: This arm of the Mediterranean lies between the Greek mainland and Anatolia, dividing the two nations.

clue.text: Needlework of note, first time out

indicators.note: out says the letter for time is removed from the note

parts.note: a crotchet is a musical note, a quarter note

indicators.note: first says only the opening letter of the word time is wanted

explanation.surface: A piece of needlework of some distinction, being tried for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first time out' removes the first T from CROTCHET; a crotchet is the British name for a quarter note.
explanation.definitionFit: Crochet is handicraft made by looping yarn with a hooked needle, a form of needlework.

clue.text: Cook travelling first by railway

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters of the next word moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A chef journeys first class by train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges FIRST into STIRF.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook food quickly over high heat in a wok is this verb, so it is a kind of cooking.

clue.text: No agent ordered as much as can be carried

definitions.text: as much as can be carried

indicators.note: ordered suggests the letters being arranged anew

explanation.surface: No agent placed an order for as much as could be carried.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's carrying capacity is measured as its weight in tons, the load it can hold.

clue.text: About 100 before end of day stick to processing waste

parts.note: re means about or concerning
C is the Roman numeral for 100

indicators.note: end of says to take only the final letter of the word day

parts.note: to cling is to stick to

explanation.surface: Instructions about keeping at something for 100 days before stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of day' gives Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Reprocessing used materials so they can be made into new goods is what this means.
